# Generated by `bazel run //platform/buildScripts:plugin-model-tool` - do not edit.
#
# What the JPS-to-Bazel converter reads besides the project model, in one file with one section per table.
# A section a hermetic run cannot see is a section that run decides the other way, so one declaration -
# `@community//build:dev_dist_plugin_tables` - names this file for every run that reads it.
#
# `[content_vetoes]` - plugin or product layouts exclude paths from these modules, so their raw output
# cannot be handed to `PackContentModuleJar`. One module name per row.
#
# `[content_candidate_overrides]` - whether a module can be packed as a plain `lib/modules/<module>.jar` is a
# repo-global AND over what every plugin's own model states, and the converter folds it. These are the
# community modules a community-only checkout would fold differently, because the plugins that decide them
# are in the ultimate half: `+` is a candidate, `-` is not, and the sign is the whole-repo answer either
# way. A `+` row names the module libraries merged into its jar after the module name, because the fold
# agrees on that set as well and a community-only checkout cannot see it. The converter states these rows
# and records them in `bazel-targets.json`; this run only writes them out.
#
# `[descriptor_population]` - which (plugin, layout variant) a `dev_dist_plugin_descriptor` target exists for,
# one `<main module>` or `<main module>/<variant>` per row. The converter emits one target per row, beside
# the plugin.
#
# `[plugin_jar_placement]` - where a plugin puts its own jars, for the plugin whose layout renames its
# directory or its main jar. Three tab-separated tokens: `<main module>`, `<directory>`, `<main jar name>`.
# A plugin with no row takes the convention `intellij.a.b` -> `a-b` and `a-b.jar`, which is what
# `PluginLayout` gives a plugin that renames neither. The converter needs both names to state a jar of the
# plugin in the dev-distribution recipe, and no project model holds either.
#
# `[plugin_descriptor_residue]` - what a plugin's patched descriptor needs that the convention does not
# give, for the plugin that reads a descriptor through an `xi:include` or whose `PluginLayout` deviates. The
# key is `<main module>` or `<main module>/<variant>`, because a descriptor deviation is a fact about one
# layout variant. A plugin the section does not name is pure convention.
#
# One row per fact, tab separated: the key, the field name, then that field's own tokens. So one key states
# several rows, and a flat reader needs no nesting rule. A field whose value is a list states one row per
# item, and the rows keep the order the patch applies them in. A flag field states the key and the field
# name alone. Tabs, because a marker row states a `:` and a space.
#
# The fields: `descriptor` states a load path and the project-relative path that answers it;
# `library_descriptor` states a load path, the owning module and the library name; `refused_content_module`
# and `separate_jar` each state one content module; `marker` states one marker-table row of the layout's raw
# text patch; `version_suffix` states what the layout appends to the build version; `no_embedding`,
# `exact_version` and `retain_product_descriptor` are flags.
#
# Every path here is project-relative, and no row is a Bazel label. The converter resolves a path to a label
# itself, which is what lets the community half decide alone: a path outside `community/` is a path a
# community package cannot name, and the community half then emits no target for that plugin.
#
# The plugin directory and the main jar name are not rows here. `[plugin_jar_placement]` states
# both, for every plugin that renames either, and the converter reads them there.
